title: Purchasing Assistant
description:
Purchasing Assistant
Desford LE9 (Onsite role)
Initial 12-month contract - likely to extend for the right Person!
Hours: 37.5 a week (typical work patterns are Mon-Fri: 07:00-15:00 /07 30 /08:00-16:00)
Up to £18.75 PAYE hourly rate plus holiday and pension contribution OR Umbrella hourly rates up to £25.66

Have you recently worked in a Purchasing role where you were responsible for raising purchase orders? Are you used to liaising with global suppliers? Do you pride yourself on having an excellent eye for detail? If yes, this could be the opportunity you have been waiting for .
We re looking for a Purchasing Assistant to join our globally renowned client s Team in Desford. This is a critical role supporting the day-to-day effectiveness of the Procurement department which demands exceptional attention to detail, energy, expertise, and dedication. As a Purchasing Assistant, you will provide comprehensive support to the facility's Purchasing function, managing requisitions, raising orders, and collaborating with Suppliers along with internal departments to address and resolve issues.

What will the Purchasing Assistant do?
- Generate and manage purchase orders to fulfil business requirements
- Update and maintain purchasing systems with accurate and up-to-date pricing details
- Resolve invoice discrepancies and ensure timely payment processing
- Oversee the delivery of materials to support New Product Introduction (NPI) programs
- Build and nurture strong, collaborative relationships with suppliers
- Perform analytical and administrative tasks to support purchasing-related strategic initiatives and provide accurate data to assist Buyers.
- Work closely with other teams to understand and meet customer requirements
- Extract data from internal systems and generate various reports for operational support
- Ensure continuous compliance with organisational and regulatory requirements
- Assist with internal and external audit assessments as needed

What skills and experience does the Purchasing Assistant need?
- A minimum of 2 years experience in a purchasing/procurement administration environment
- Good understanding of the purchasing process, including supplier selection and onboarding, Request for Quotation (RFQ), and receipt of goods.
- Strong problem-solving skills paired with exceptional attention to detail
- Skilled in gathering and analysing data to support strategic business decisions and align with organizational objectives
- Ability to follow compliance-driven processes and procedures
- Keen & willing to learn personality and positive outlook will go a long way in this instance!
- Proficient in Microsoft Office & using ERP Systems. Desirable experience: SAP and Power BI

To apply, please submit a copy of your up to date CV clearly indicating your relevant experience. Applicants must have an existing right to work in the UK and evidence of eligibility will be required. Suitable candidates will be contacted.

The above represents a summary of the contract assignment. A full description of this contract assignment is available. A full explanation of this rate and all deductions will be explained in a key information document (KID) supplied to registered candidates.

title: HR Administrator
description:
HR Administrator - School Trust

Location: Central Trust Office, with travel to schools within the Trust

We are looking for a highly organised and proactive HR Administrator to join our friendly and supportive School Trust team. Based primarily at our central office, you will provide effective HR and administrative support across the Trust, with travel to a couple of our schools as required.

This is a varied role that would suit someone who enjoys working with people, is confident handling confidential information and has excellent attention to detail. There will also be some involvement in finance and payroll administration, although previous finance experience is not essential as training and support can be provided.

This is a temporary role working 8-4 Monday - Thursday and 8-3:30 on a Friday. To start ASAP and running until at least Christmas. They may be the option of a permanent position bhut that is not guaranteed.

Key responsibilities

Your day-to-day duties will include:

Providing general administrative support to the HR function and schools across the Trust
Maintaining accurate and up-to-date employee records and HR systems
Supporting the recruitment process, including preparing adverts, arranging interviews and completing pre-employment checks
Assisting with new starter and leaver processes
Preparing HR documentation, letters and contracts
Supporting managers and staff with general HR queries
Monitoring and maintaining records relating to sickness absence, annual leave and other employee information
Assisting with payroll administration and providing relevant information to the payroll team
Supporting basic finance administration, such as processing invoices, checking information and maintaining records
Producing reports and maintaining accurate spreadsheets and databases
Ensuring HR processes and documentation are completed accurately and on time
Liaising with staff, school leaders and external providers when required
Providing administrative support for meetings, training and other HR-related activities
Travelling occasionally to other schools within the Trust to provide on-site support

About you

We are looking for someone who is:
Highly organised with excellent attention to detail
Confident using Microsoft Office, particularly Word and Excel
Able to manage confidential and sensitive information appropriately
A strong communicator who is comfortable dealing with staff at all levels
Able to prioritise and manage a varied workload
Reliable, professional and able to work independently as well as part of a team
Previous HR or school administration experience would be advantageous, but is not essential
Some experience of finance or payroll administration would be beneficial, but is not essential

Aspire People Limited provides services as an Education Agency and an Education Employment Business. Aspire People is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of pupils and expects every candidate to share this commitment. Placements are subject, to appropriate Child Protection screening, including checks with former employers and the Disclosure and Barring Checks.

- Produce daily and weekly reports relating to staffing and operational performance.
- Liaise with agency providers to coordinate labour requirements.
- Support investigations, disciplinary meetings, and employee engagement activities through note-taking and administration.
- Manage reception and visitor processes, meeting room bookings, and site communications.

Required Knowledge & Skills

What We're Looking For
- Previous experience in an administrative, depot, operations, HR, or logistics support role.

- Excellent attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy.
- Confident communicator who can build relationships at all levels.
- Ability to handle confidential information professionally.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a supportive team where you can make a real impact on operational efficiency and employee experience.

title: Mental Health Act Administrator
description: The Mental Health Act is complex and interesting. Understanding those complexities and maintaining an interest is essential to the success of the role. This is a Band 4 role as it holds with it the delegated responsibility from the Trust Board for compliance with those complexities. The Trust expects to receive a service that delivers and is responsive not only to service demands but also to changes in legislation. The Mental Health Act Office undertakes to deliver that service, the work itself is relentless but ensures the Trusts compliance with the legalities of both the Act itself and the associated Code of Practice. Under the direction of the Senior Mental Health Act Administrator and direct management of the Deputy to the above, the Mental Health Act Administrator is expected to provide a professional, efficient and seamless service to the Trust in accordance with the provisions of the Act. Please note, previous applicants for this post need not re-apply. Receive, scrutinise and arrange rectification of statutory forms in accordance with legislation. Provide or obtain advice on MHA legislation and ensure legal and organisational reporting requirements are met. Support the Tribunal Service and MHA Managers Panel with the administration of patient hearings. Maintain monitoring systems and electronic patient records, ensuring information is accurate, current and accessible. Work collaboratively with clinical and non-clinical staff to meet local and national requirements. Complete incident reporting and support the sharing of lessons learned where appropriate. Liaise with external organisations and stakeholders within areas of responsibility. Respond professionally and sensitively to enquiries from patients, relatives and carers. Promote the Mental Health Act Office service internally and externally. Support the production and reporting of MHA data. Contribute as an integral member of the Mental Health Act Office team, providing cover for colleagues as required. Assist with staff induction, training and development, offering guidance and support where appropriate. Work flexibly to maintain effective office cover and attend occasional meetings as required.
